faqs.question: What audio components are needed for a complete smartphone audio system?
faqs.answer: A complete smartphone audio system typically includes: 1-2 MEMS microphones for voice capture (recommend SPH0641LU4H digital microphone), a micro speaker for loudspeaker applications (recommend SPS1318), and a receiver for earpiece (recommend SPS1318RA). Additional components may include audio codecs and amplifiers. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for complete system design support.
faqs.decisionGuide: Complete audio system with microphone, speaker, and receiver.

faqs.question: How do I optimize microphone placement in smartphones?
faqs.answer: For optimal microphone performance: 1) Place primary microphone near bottom for voice pickup; 2) Position secondary microphone at top for noise cancellation; 3) Keep microphones away from speakers to prevent feedback; 4) Use acoustic mesh for dust protection; 5) Ensure proper sealing to prevent wind noise. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for microphone placement guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Strategic placement for voice pickup and noise rejection.

faqs.question: What speaker enclosure design is recommended?
faqs.answer: For best speaker performance: 1) Maximize enclosure volume within device constraints; 2) Use sealed enclosure for better bass response; 3) Include acoustic vents for pressure equalization; 4) Mount speaker on rigid surface to reduce vibration; 5) Consider waterproof membrane for water-resistant designs. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for enclosure design support.
faqs.decisionGuide: Maximize enclosure volume and ensure proper sealing.

faqs.question: How do I prevent echo in speakerphone mode?
faqs.answer: To prevent echo in speakerphone mode: 1) Use acoustic echo cancellation (AEC) algorithm in audio codec; 2) Position microphone away from speaker; 3) Implement proper acoustic isolation; 4) Use directional microphone to reduce speaker pickup; 5) Tune AEC parameters for your specific design. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for echo cancellation guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Use AEC algorithm and proper microphone placement.

faqs.question: What is the typical power consumption of smartphone audio components?
faqs.answer: Typical power consumption: MEMS microphones 150-200μA, micro speakers driven with 0.5-1W amplifier (efficiency dependent), receivers 10-20mW. Total audio subsystem power is typically 50-100mW during active use. Low power modes reduce consumption to microamps when inactive. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for power optimization guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Total audio power typically 50-100mW during active use.

faqs.question: Which sensors are best for IoT environmental monitoring?
faqs.answer: For IoT environmental monitoring, we recommend: SPL06-007 pressure sensor for altitude and weather, SPA2032 accelerometer for motion detection, and SPAC2032 combo sensor for complete motion tracking. These sensors feature I2C interface and ultra-low power for battery-operated IoT devices. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for IoT sensor selection guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Pressure and motion sensors for IoT monitoring.

faqs.question: How do I maximize battery life in IoT sensors?
faqs.answer: To maximize battery life: 1) Use low-power sensors with sleep modes; 2) Optimize sampling rate (e.g., 1Hz instead of 100Hz); 3) Implement batch data transmission; 4) Use interrupts instead of polling; 5) Consider energy harvesting for extended operation. With proper optimization, 2+ year battery life is achievable. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for power optimization guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Optimize sampling rates and use sleep modes.

faqs.question: What is relates to Goertek pressure sensors?
faqs.answer: Goertek pressure sensors offer excellent accuracy: SPL06-007 provides ±0.06hPa relative accuracy for ~0.5m altitude resolution, while SPL07-003 offers ±0.03hPa for ~0.25m resolution. Absolute accuracy is ±1hPa. This enables accurate altitude tracking for drones, fitness applications, and weather monitoring. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for pressure sensor selection.
faqs.decisionGuide: 0.03-0.06hPa accuracy for precise altitude measurement.

faqs.question: How do I interface multiple sensors on the same I2C bus?
faqs.answer: To interface multiple sensors on I2C bus: 1) Ensure each sensor has unique I2C address (most Goertek sensors have configurable addresses); 2) Use proper pull-up resistors (4.7kΩ typical); 3) Keep bus capacitance under 400pF; 4) Use level shifters if mixing 3.3V and 1.8V devices; 5) Implement proper error handling. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for I2C design guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Use unique addresses and proper pull-up resistors.

faqs.question: What is relates to combo sensors over discrete sensors?
faqs.answer: Combo sensors integrate multiple sensing functions in one package, providing: 1) Reduced PCB space (single 2.5x3mm vs multiple packages); 2) Lower total cost; 3) Simplified procurement and inventory; 4) Guaranteed sensor alignment; 5) Single interface for all sensors. 6-axis combos include accel+gyro, 9-axis add magnetometer. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for combo sensor selection.
faqs.decisionGuide: Combo sensors save space, cost, and simplify design.

faqs.question: What automotive qualifications do Goertek components have?
faqs.answer: Goertek automotive components are qualified to AEC-Q100 Grade 1 standards, operating from -40°C to +125°C. PPAP Level 3 documentation is available. Components meet automotive EMC requirements including CISPR 25 and ISO 11452. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for qualification documentation.
faqs.decisionGuide: AEC-Q100 Grade 1 qualified for automotive.

faqs.question: What is PPAP and why is it important?
faqs.answer: PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) is a standardized process in automotive industry to ensure supplier components meet all customer engineering design and specification requirements. PPAP Level 3 includes design records, test results, process capability studies, and other documentation. It is required for all automotive production parts. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for PPAP support.
faqs.decisionGuide: PPAP Level 3 required for automotive production.

faqs.question: How do I ensure EMC compliance for automotive audio?
faqs.answer: For automotive EMC compliance: 1) Use AEC-Q100 qualified components with built-in EMI protection; 2) Implement proper power supply filtering; 3) Use shielded cables for audio connections; 4) Follow CISPR 25 and ISO 11452 standards; 5) Test early in development to identify issues. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for EMC design guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Use qualified components and follow automotive EMC standards.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Grade 1 and Grade 2 AEC-Q100?
faqs.answer: AEC-Q100 Grade 1 components are qualified for -40°C to +125°C operating temperature, suitable for most automotive applications including under-hood locations. Grade 2 covers -40°C to +105°C, suitable for passenger compartment. Grade 1 provides wider operating range and higher reliability margins. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for grade selection guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Grade 1 for under-hood, Grade 2 for passenger compartment.

faqs.question: How long is the supply guarantee for automotive components?
faqs.answer: Goertek provides long-term supply guarantees for automotive components, typically 10-15 years from production start. This ensures continuity of supply for vehicle production and service requirements. Full traceability and change notification are provided. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for supply agreement details.
faqs.decisionGuide: 10-15 year supply guarantee for automotive.

faqs.question: Which microphone is best for voice assistant applications?
faqs.answer: For voice assistants, we recommend SPH0645LM4H (66dB SNR digital) for premium applications or SPH0641LU4H (64dB SNR digital) for cost-effective designs. Digital microphones with PDM output are preferred for direct connection to voice processors. Use multiple microphones in array configuration for far-field performance. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for voice assistant design guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: High SNR digital microphones for voice assistants.

faqs.question: How many microphones do I need for far-field voice pickup?
faqs.answer: For far-field voice pickup: 2 microphones provide basic noise reduction; 4 microphones enable good beamforming for 3-5 meter range; 6+ microphones provide excellent performance for larger rooms. Array spacing of 20-40mm is typical. More microphones improve directionality and noise rejection. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for array design guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: 4-6 microphones for good far-field performance.

faqs.question: What is beamforming and how does it help?
faqs.answer: Beamforming is a signal processing technique that uses multiple microphones to create a directional pickup pattern. It enhances voice capture from the desired direction while rejecting noise from other directions. This improves far-field performance and wake-word recognition in noisy environments. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for beamforming implementation guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Beamforming improves directionality and noise rejection.

faqs.question: How do I prevent false wake-word triggers?
faqs.answer: To prevent false wake-word triggers: 1) Use high SNR microphones for clean audio capture; 2) Implement microphone array for spatial filtering; 3) Tune wake-word algorithm threshold; 4) Use adaptive noise cancellation; 5) Consider multi-stage wake-word detection. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for wake-word optimization guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: Use high SNR mics and proper algorithm tuning.

faqs.question: What is the optimal microphone spacing for arrays?
faqs.answer: Optimal microphone spacing depends on application: 20-30mm spacing for compact devices like smart speakers; 40-60mm for larger devices; 80-100mm for far-field applications. Smaller spacing provides wider beam but less directionality. Larger spacing improves directionality but may cause spatial aliasing at high frequencies. Contact BeiLuo FAE team for array spacing guidance.
faqs.decisionGuide: 20-40mm typical spacing for voice applications.
